figures.item: EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directives Implementation Regulations, S.L. 123.187 (L.N. 411 of 2018, amended L.N. 348 of 2019 and 29 of 2020): "associated enterprise" threshold for votes, capital or profits (CFC and interest rules). Replaced by 50% for the hybrid mismatch rules.
figures.quote: twenty- five per cent (25%) or more of the profits of that entity

figures.item: Cap. 123 art. 2(1) "resident in Malta" for a body of persons: managed and controlled in Malta; and a company incorporated in Malta on or after this date is always resident (other Maltese-incorporated companies from 1 January 1995).
figures.quote: provided that a company incorporated in Malta on or after 1st July 1994 shall be resident in Malta

figures.item: Cap. 123 art. 27D(1): a resident trustee of an authorised trust holding only investment income (royalties, dividends, capital gains, interest, rents) may irrevocably elect to have trust income taxed as if derived by a Malta company (art. 56(6) rate, dividend treatment for distributions). The election form goes to the Commissioner within this period from establishment or appointment of a resident trustee, whichever is later.
figures.quote: not later than thirty days from the date of the establishment of such trust

figures.item: Foundations (Income Tax) Regulations, S.L. 123.114 (L.N. 312 of 2010), reg. 4: by default a foundation is taxed like a company (distributions treated as dividends); its administrators may irrevocably elect by written notice to be taxed under the trust rules instead. No number.
figures.quote: irrevocably elect that a foundation

figures.item: Duty on Documents and Transfers Act, Cap. 364, art. 32(1): duty on transfers of immovable property, including the declaration of a transfer causa mortis (on death), for deaths on or after 23 November 1999: five euro for every one hundred euro or part of the higher of consideration and value. Printed as "five euro (5.00) for every one hundred euro (100)"; not printed as a percentage.
figures.value: five euro per one hundred euro
figures.quote: a duty of five euro (5.00) for every one

figures.item: Duty on Documents and Transfers Act, Cap. 364, art. 35(1)(a)(i): on a transfer causa mortis of the deceased's ordinary residence, the first slice of its value is not taken into account (or a greater amount if prescribed); pro rata where the home was not fully owned or passes to several heirs.
figures.quote: The first thirty-five thousand euro (35,000)

figures.item: Duty on Documents and Transfers Act, Cap. 364, art. 35(2)(i): where the deceased's ordinary residence is occupied at death by an heir as their ordinary residence, duty on that heir's share of the value above EUR 35,000 and up to EUR 200,000 is three euro fifty per one hundred euro.
figures.quote: three euro and fifty cents (€3.50) for every one hundred euro (€100)

figures.item: Duty on Documents and Transfers Act, Cap. 364, art. 35(2)(i): upper end of the slice of the dwelling house value taxed at the reduced EUR 3.50 per EUR 100 rate (value above it bears the normal rate).
figures.quote: which exceeds thirty-five thousand euro (€35,000) but not two hundred thousand euro (€200,000)

figures.item: Duty on Documents and Transfers Act, Cap. 364, art. 35(2)(iii): no duty is levied at the time of the transfer causa mortis where the deceased's ordinary residence passes to the surviving spouse or cohabitant. Art. 35(2)(v) gives the same for the ordinary residence passing to descendants in the direct line, if its conditions are met. No number.
figures.value: no duty at the time of the transfer
figures.quote: the beneficiary of such residence is the surviving spouse or cohabitant, no duty shall be levied at the time of the transfer

figures.item: Duty on Documents and Transfers Act, Cap. 364, art. 35(1)(b): the value of a usufruct bequeathed to the surviving spouse or cohabitant is not taken into account for duty. No number.
figures.quote: The value of the usufruct of any property chargeable under this Act bequeathed

figures.item: Duty on Documents and Transfers Act, Cap. 364, art. 42(1): duty on transfers of marketable securities (including the notice of a transfer causa mortis of company shares under art. 45): two euro for every one hundred euro of the higher of consideration and real value. Printed in words only.
figures.value: two euro per one hundred euro
figures.quote: A duty of two euro for every one hundred euro or part

figures.item: Duty on Documents and Transfers Act, Cap. 364, art. 42(2)(a) and (b): where the company (or a company it holds) has 75 percent or more of non-current assets in immovable property, the share duty is increased by three euro per one hundred euro. Printed in words only.
figures.value: three euro per one hundred euro
figures.quote: shall be increased by three euro for every one hundred euro

figures.item: Duty on Documents and Transfers Act, Cap. 364, art. 41C(1): transfer of a registered family business (Family Business Act, Cap. 565) as a going concern by an individual to family members, including a commercial tenement used in the business for at least three years: reduced duty on the first slice of the property value. Rate printed in words: three euro and fifty cents per one hundred euro.
figures.quote: duty shall be charged on the first five hundred thousand euro (€500,000)

figures.item: Duty on Documents and Transfers Act, Cap. 364, art. 41C(2): transfer by an individual to family members of shares or interests in a partnership, trust or foundation held in a registered family business: the first slice of value is not taken into account (or a greater amount if prescribed). Conditions include more than 85 percent family control and a Commissioner certificate.
figures.quote: no account shall be taken of the first one hundred and fifty thousand euro (€150,000)

figures.item: Duty on Documents and Transfers Act, Cap. 364, art. 41C(1) provisos: if the property is transferred inter vivos or stops being used in the business within this period from acquisition, the duty saved becomes payable.
figures.quote: during the first three years from the date of acquisition

figures.item: Income Tax Act art. 5A(5)(a): final tax on transfers of Malta immovable property made on or after 1 January 2015, as a share of the transfer value (general case; many special rates exist).
figures.quote: shall be chargeable at the rate of 8% of the transfer value

figures.item: Income Tax Act art. 5A(5)(b): where the property sold was inherited (transfer causa mortis after 24 November 1992) or donated more than five years earlier, the tax is this rate on the excess of transfer value over acquisition value, unless the seller elects otherwise in the deed. Not the 12% of transfer value in art. 5A(5)(a).
figures.quote: shall be chargeable at 12% of the excess, if any, of the transfer value over its acquisition value

figures.item: Income Tax Act art. 5A(5)(c): property inherited causa mortis before 25 November 1992 (or sold by judicial auction): tax at this rate of the transfer value.
figures.quote: shall be chargeable at the rate of 7% of the transfer value. (d)

figures.item: Global Residence Programme Rules, rule 6(1)(f): special tax status ends if the individual stays in any other jurisdiction for more than one hundred and eighty-three days in a calendar year. Printed in words.
figures.quote: stays in any other jurisdiction for more than one hundred and eighty-three days in a calendar year

figures.item: Income Tax Act art. 4(1) proviso (ii): no tax on capital gains arising outside Malta for a person not ordinarily resident or not domiciled in Malta, even if remitted. No number.
figures.quote: no tax shall be payable on capital gains arising outside Malta to a person who is not ordinarily resident in Malta or not domiciled

figures.item: Income Tax Act art. 4(1) proviso (i): for a person not ordinarily resident or not domiciled in Malta, foreign income is taxed only on the amount received in Malta (remittance basis). No number.
figures.value: taxed on amount received in Malta
figures.quote: the tax shall be payable on the amount received in Malta
